To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

zinc efflux activators (ZnEAs) are a novel family of TetR‐family metalloregulators that activate transcription of metal efflux genes, and that the ZnEAs SczAs are the first TetR family regulators that are activated by intracellular metal sensing.
the zinc efflux regulator, SczA, is a TetR‐family zinc‐sensing transcriptional regulator, and the A‐ and the B‐sites of SczA are required for zinc sensing and activation of czc expression.
zinc is a critical nutrient for Streptococcus (S.) pneumoniae and other bacterial pathogens, yet high levels of zinc can inhibit growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of zinc toxicity and zinc resistance in pathogenic bacteria.
the zinc efflux activators SczAs, and the zinc efflux regulator CzcD in S. pneumonia.
zinc homeostasis in S. pneumonia, and the role of zinc in the pathogenesis of pneumococcal disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SczA is the zinc‐responsive activator of czcD, and that the A‐site serves as the intracellular zinc sensor.
the A‐site is the intracellular zinc sensing site in all SczAs, while the B‐site is the extracellular zinc sensing site.
the S. pneumoniae zinc efflux activators, SczA, binds two zinc ions in the regulatory domain, and that both metal binding sites are required for transcriptional regulation of the czcD operon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

zinc sensing in S. pneumonia is mediated by a homodimeric transcription factor that has two zinc binding sites, one of which functions as the intracellular sensing site and the other as a regulatory site.
we have identified and characterized a zinc‐sensing transcriptional regulator that protects S. pneumoniae from intracellular zinc intoxication.
we have identified a new zinc sensing protein in S. pneumonia and determined the structure of this new zinc sensor protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zinc efflux activators SczA and CzcD are essential for S. pneumonia survival during zinc intoxication, and are potential targets for the design of new antibacterial agents.
the zinc‐sensing mechanism in SczA is distinct from that of other TetR‐family regulators, and is a novel zinc sensing mechanism.
SczA is a zinc‐activated transcriptional regulator of the czcD operon that protects S. pneumoniae serotype‐2 D39 against zinc intoxication.
